I would reclassify Ryan’s absence from **SC to UA**, add a factual note, and submit the list before the 12:00 payroll deadline.

### Why UA is the correct code

- **SC** is inappropriate because Ryan states that he was not ill.
- **BRV** is inappropriate under the supplied definition because it covers the death of a listed relative. His sister gave birth; nobody died.
- **DEP** is inappropriate because a sibling is not one of the listed relationships unless that sibling lives in the employee’s household. Ryan is recorded as living alone, and his sister lives in Castleford.
- Ryan had not booked the absence in advance. Therefore, under the definitions provided, it falls into **UA: any other absence that was not booked in advance**.

The fact that Ryan telephoned Gary at 05:40 is important mitigating context, but calling in does not turn the absence into sickness, dependants’ leave or bereavement leave under the stated rules.

### What I would record and do

I would add a concise note such as:

> Absent to support his sister during unexpected premature labour and childbirth. Ryan informed Gary at 05:40 that he could not attend his 06:00 shift. He reported no illness. His sister does not live at his address.

I would then submit the list on time. Because Ryan already has a UA from 18 August and his probation does not end until 12 November, this will be treated as his second UA. The stated payroll process will therefore produce and send the one-week-notice termination letter on Friday.

Because that is a significant consequence, I would also email Ryan, the HR Manager and Gary as soon as possible, explaining:

- why the code has been changed;
- that the second-UA probation rule is expected to trigger the letter; and
- that Ryan’s act of notifying Gary and the family circumstances can be considered in any subsequent HR review or mitigation.

I would not leave the absence coded as SC merely to avoid the termination outcome, invent a family-emergency category, or treat the free-text note as though it changes payroll or probation. If Pennine has a separate authorised-family-emergency policy, that would need proper managerial consideration, but none is provided in the hypothetical.
